sentences: Treewidth measures how a graph can be decomposed into small overlapping pieces organized by a tree.
The source asks for polylogarithmic bounds on treewidth under a particular structural setting.
Such a bound would imply that large graphs in that setting retain relatively small decomposition width.
This matters because many otherwise difficult graph tasks become easier when treewidth is controlled.

The inherited title does not identify the hypotheses or the parameter inside the logarithm, so no universal treewidth estimate can be asserted until the seminar's precise graph class and quantitative target are recovered.
